# Independent audit: global parameter optimality from the contact martingale

Source read in full: `candidate b2578378c7102b3c`, Sections 1–6. Verdict: **PASS**. In particular the strictness step is valid for a FIXED fiber-interior mark; it does not require the mark to remain globally deepest for the new parameter.

## 1. The global inequality and equality conditions

The row change of measure is correctly normalized. For R=U/L,

    E_(bar_rho_i)R=E_(rho_i)U/L_i<=U(Y_i)/L_i.

The inequality is Jensen for U under the TILTED row whose mean is Y_i. Applying log Jensen under the ORIGINAL row then summing gives the claimed global multiplicative inequality. This order matters; replacing the tilted mean by the original-row mean would not be valid.

Both parts of the stated deficit are nonnegative. The entropy orientation is correct: KL(bar_rho_i||tau_i)=log b_i-E_(bar_rho_i)log R. Equality forces BOTH affine Jensen equality for U and an almost surely constant ratio U/L on every positive row. Thus normalized U with U(Y_i)<=L_i at every positive row agrees with L almost everywhere under the original mixed measure. Continuity upgrades this to every point in every sampled positive fiber, including boundaries. No equality between unsampled extensions is needed.

The equivalent log-maximization statement follows directly from the same inequality and its equality conditions. The radial-cone dual follows by Jensen for h+cL, with exact cancellation of cL. The converse is the independently audited finite-source continuous-target convex-order construction. Exact moving-plane secants are radial directions, so the proof covers switching affine pieces without differentiating across creases.

## 2. Fixed-mark strictness: an independent proof

Fix an actual mark Y=(p,y), with y in the interior of its positive fiber K_p. Keep the bodies and covariance norm G fixed. For a scalar s>=0 let D(s) be the infimum of the masses of caps

    a.(z-p)+u.(X-y)>=-s G(u),

together with the pure-base caps. Write B=b_base(p). Monotonicity gives D(s_2)>=D(s_1) for s_2>s_1. If D(s_1)<B and D(s_2)=B, strictness is immediate. Suppose D(s_2)<B. The following uniform near-minimizer proof avoids relying on attainment at the new scalar.

Normalize |u|=1 for every nonvertical near-minimizing cap. Choose eta>0 with D(s_2)+2eta<B. For all sufficiently accurate near-minimizers their mass is at most B-eta. Such a cap cannot have full own capture: the whole-own-fiber lemma gives mass at least B. For completeness, the sampled lower support l_z(u)=min_(K_z)u.X is a convex array by actual compatibility. A finite affine minorant touching it at p gives a closed base halfspace through p whose every full fiber lies in any cap containing all of K_p. This proves the required B lower bound without cap regularity.

Let t=u.y-s_2G(u) be the own threshold and l=l_p(u). Lowering the ambient threshold by t-l gives a full-own cap, of mass at least B. The all-fiber slab upper bound is uniform in u and in the arbitrary base tilt: a threshold displacement h changes at most C h mixed volume, because there are finitely many bounded positive fibers. Hence

    t-l>=eta/C.

On the other side, since s_2>=0 and y is a fixed interior point,

    h_(K_p)(u)-t>=h_(K_p)(u)-u.y>=rho>0,

uniformly in unit u. Both the new threshold and the old one u.y-s_1G(u), and the entire strip between them, therefore stay in a compact set of proper sections bounded away from both supports. Section volume has a uniform positive lower bound there (also for nonsmooth K_p), and G has a uniform positive minimum on the unit sphere. Reducing the scalar from s_2 to s_1 removes at least

    c (s_2-s_1) min_(|u|=1)G(u)>0

from the OWN fiber of every such near-minimizer, and removes nonnegative volume from the others. Comparing their old cap masses and then taking the near-minimizer limit proves D(s_1)<D(s_2).

The argument is valid for d=1, where proper section density is constant, and for arbitrary nonsmooth higher-dimensional fibers. It retains pure-base boundaries and all unbounded base tilts. The source's shorter proof via proper-gap attainment is therefore sound and has exactly the claimed fixed-mark scope.

## 3. Actual global parameter conclusion

At the old proper marks, increasing U(Y_i) strictly increases the scalar buffer because E_(K_(p_i))(y_i)>0 and epsilon>0. The multiplicative inequality supplies at least one nondecreased mark, giving global fixed-body parameter minimality. If a competing normalized parameter had global maximum no greater than Q, the fixed-mark strictness just proved would force U(Y_i)<=L_i at EVERY positive source. The equality theorem then forces U=L on all sampled fibers.

This establishes the claimed uniqueness for the fixed body, epsilon, mass and covariance. It makes no statement about changing the body, identifies no physical separator, and supplies no Gamma payment. The one-gradient fixed-body obstruction remains consistent with every conclusion.
